'''Marcin Śmiglecki''' ([[Latin]]: ''Martinus Smiglecius'' or ''Leopolitanus,'' {{langx|lt|Martynas Smigleckis}};<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mokslasvu.mb.vu.lt/LT.php?content=publication&Id=166 |title=Smigleckis, Martynas |website=www.mokslasvu.mb.vu.lt |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722153905/http://www.mokslasvu.mb.vu.lt/LT.php?content=publication&Id=166 |archive-date=2011-07-22}} </ref> 11 November 1564 &ndash; 26 or 28 July 1618) was a Polish [[Jesuit]] philosopher and logician,<ref name=Schmitt>{{cite book |editor1-last=Schmitt |editor1-first=C. B. |editor2-last=Skinner |editor2-first=Quentin |title=The Cambridge History of Renaissance Philosophy |date=1988 |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=9781139055420 |page=158}}</ref><ref name="Haaparanta">{{cite book |editor1-last=Haaparanta |editor1-first=Leila|editor1-link= Leila Haaparanta |title=The Development of Modern Logic |date=2008 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |isbn=978-0195137316 |page=89}}</ref> known for his erudite [[Scholasticism|scholastic]] ''Logica''.

==Life==
He was born on 11 November 1564<ref name="PWN">{{cite web |title=Śmiglecki Marcin, Encyklopedia PWN |url=https://encyklopedia.pwn.pl/haslo/Smiglecki-Marcin;3984159.html |publisher=[[Polish Scientific Publishers PWN|PWN]] |website=encyklopedia.pwn.pl|access-date=23 August 2018 |language=pl}}</ref> in [[Lwów]] (Leopolis) in the [[Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569)|Kingdom of Poland]] (now Lviv, [[Ukraine]]). He used the surname Lwowczyk, or Leopolitanus, and later adopted the name Śmiglecki or Smiglecius (after the town of [[Śmigiel]], from which his family originated). He attended the Jesuit school in [[Pułtusk]] and until 1586 studied in [[Rome]], where he joined the Jesuit order in 1581. His education was financed by the prominent Polish statesman [[Jan Zamojski]]. He obtained a master's degree in philosophy and a doctor's degree in theology at the [[Vilnius University#Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth|Academy of Vilnius]], and taught philosophy and theology there.<ref name=Roncalia/>

In 1599 he took part in a public disputation with the Protestants [[Marcin Janicki]] and [[Daniel Mikołajewski (theologian)|Daniel Mikołajewski]]. It was recorded by Martin Gratian Gertich.<ref>Edmund de Schweinitz, ''History of the Church Known as the Unitas Fratrum Or the Unity of the Brethren'' (1885), note p. 473.</ref>

He spent the last 20 years of his life teaching in the colleges of Pułtusk, [[Poznań]], [[Kraków]] and [[Kalisz]]. He died in Kalisz on 26 or 28 July 1618.<ref name=Roncalia>{{cite book |last1=Roncaglia |first1=Gino |title=Smiglecius on entia rationis |url=http://dspace.unitus.it/bitstream/2067/460/1/Smiglecius_on_entia_rationis.pdf|pages=1–4}}</ref><ref name="PWN"/>

==Publications==
His early works include:<ref name=Roncalia/>
*''Examen fidei sectariorum seu Notae verae et apostolicae fidei an scilicet fides, quam sectarij praedicant, sit vera et apostolica Joannis Twardowski'' (Wilno, 1594)
*''Opisanie dispvtaciey nowogrodzkiey, ktorą miał X. Marcin Smiglecki, Societatis Iesv z Janem Licyniuszem, ministrem nowokrzczeńskim o przedwiecznym bostwie Syna Bożego 24 i 25 Ianuarii w roku 1594'' (Wilno, 1594)
*''O Bostwie Przedwiecznym Syna Bozego Swiadectwa Pisma świętego do trzech przednieyszych Artykułow zebrane Przeciwko wszystkim Pana Jezusa Chrystusa nieprzyiacielom'' (Wilno, 1595)
*''Absurda Synodu Torunskiego'' (Wilno, 1596)
*''O lichwie y trzech przednieyszych kontraktach, wyderkowym, czynszowym y towarzystwa kupieckiego'' (Krakow, 1596)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lituanus.org/1981_2/81_2_01.htm|title=A Historic View of the University of Vilnius - Tomas Venclova|access-date=2008-12-31|archive-date=2021-06-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210623222449/http://www.lituanus.org/1981_2/81_2_01.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=Roncalia/> 
*''Zachariae prophetae pro Christi divinitate illustre testimonium adversus Fausti Socini'' (Wilno, 1596)
*''Dysputacya Wileńska ktorą miał [...] Marcin Smiglecki [...] Z Ministrami Ewangelickimi 2. Junii w Roku 1599 O iedney Widomey Głowie Kościoła Bożego Wydana'' (Wilno, 1599/1600?) 
*''O ledney Widomey Glowie Kosciola Bozego'' (Wilno, 1600)
Later works include:
*''Vana sine viribus ira ministrorum evangelicorum: seu Refutatio vani cujusdam Epichirematis, missionem ministrorum evangelicorum propugnantis'' (Koln, 1611)
*''Nova monstra novi arianismi, seu Absurdae haereses a novis Arianis in Poloniam importatae'' (Nissae, 1612) 
*''Verbum caro factum seu De divina verbo incarnato natura: Ex primo Evangelii S. Joannis capite, adversus novorum Arianorum errores'' (Krakow, 1613)
*''Nodus Gordius seu De vocatione ministrorum sisputatio: In qua decem demonstrationibus ostenditur ministros Evangelicos non esse veros verbi Dei & sacramentorum ministros'' (Ingolstadt, 1613)
*''Refutatio vanae dissolutionis nodi, gordii de vocatione ministrorum, Joanne Volkelio ministro Arriano tentatae'' (Krakow, 1614)
*''De baptismo adversus Hieronymum Moscorovium Arianum, liber unus'' (Krakow, 1615)
*''De Christo, vero et naturali Dei Filio, ejusdemque pro peccatis nostris satisfactione libri duo adversus impia dogmata V. Smalcii. ... Accessit Responio ad examinationem centum errorum Smalcio objectorum ab eodem Smalcio editam'' (Krakow, 1615)
*''De erroribus novorum Arianorum libri duo. Adversus responsum Valentini Smalcii, quod dedit pro novis Arianorum suorum monstris'' (Krakow, 1615)
*''De ordinatione sacerdotum in ecclesia Romana. Adversus Jacobi Zaborovii calviniani ministri dissertationem'' (Krakow, 1617)
*''De notis ministrorum libri duo, oppositi Jacobi Zaborowii, in coetu Calvinistico ministri, responsioni futili ad nodum Gordium'' (Krakow, 1617)
*''Logica'' (Ingolstadt, 1618)

==The ''Logica''==
Marcin Śmiglecki's "Logica", first published in 1618 in [[Ingolstadt]], was reprinted several times, in particular at [[University of Oxford|Oxford]] in 1634, 1638, and 1658,<ref name=Roncalia/> being used there as a textbook.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.unesco.org/webworld/mdm/visite/vilnius/knygos/knygos/logika/migle/anglu/emmigle.htm |title=Smiglecki M. Logica… |website=www.unesco.org |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606232845/http://www.unesco.org/webworld/mdm/visite/vilnius/knygos/knygos/logika/migle/anglu/emmigle.htm |archive-date=2011-06-06}} </ref> It harked back to [[Gregory of Rimini]], discussing [[mental proposition]]s.<ref>R. J. Ashworth, ''Traditional Logic'', pp. 160-1 in Charles B. Schmitt, Quentin Skinner (editors), ''The Cambridge History of Renaissance Philosophy'' (1990).</ref> As a textbook author his reputation survived in the satirical poem ''The Logicians Refuted'',<ref>[[:s:The Logicians Refuted]]</ref> attributed to both [[Jonathan Swift]] and [[Oliver Goldsmith]]. [[Samuel Johnson]], writing in 1751 as a fictitious correspondent in ''[[The Rambler]]'',  claimed that as a student he "slept every night with Śmiglecki on my pillow."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.org/stream/worksofsamueljoh05johniala/worksofsamueljoh05johniala_djvu.txt|title = The works of Samuel Johnson : In twelve volumes|year = 1792}}</ref>

==Views==
In a live controversy of the time, Śmiglecki sided with [[Benedict Pereira]] against [[Giuseppe Biancani]]. The issue was the status of [[mathematical proof]] in physics, where Pereyra denied mathematics an essential status.<ref>Paolo Mancosu, ''Philosophy of Mathematics and Mathematical Practice in the Seventeenth Century'' (1996), p. 13 and p. 19.</ref>
